title: The electromagnetic spectrum
target: Relate electromagnetic wavelength, frequency and propagation.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has frequency 5.0 × 10⁸ Hz. Use c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. What is wavelength?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Vacuum light has wavelength 750 nm. Use c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. What is frequency?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which sequence goes from longer to shorter electromagnetic wavelength?
cpa.guide: The standard spectrum progresses from radio through infrared and visible to ultraviolet and higher frequencies.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: In vacuum, which has the shorter wavelength: a microwave or an X-ray?
options: They must have equal wavelength because their speeds match.
cpa.guide: Higher-frequency X-rays have shorter wavelengths at the same vacuum speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which signal can cross an ideal vacuum without a material medium?
options: A pressure sound wave in air.
A wave on a rope with no rope present.
An ocean surface wave with no water present.
cpa.guide: Electromagnetic waves propagate in vacuum; mechanical waves require a medium.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An astronaut sees a distant flash across empty space. Which conclusion is appropriate?
options: Sound and light both require air on the path.
The flash proves sound travels faster.
Light transported all the source matter to the observer.
Light can arrive through vacuum; an ordinary sound wave cannot travel that empty path.
cpa.guide: Distinguish electromagnetic propagation from mechanical sound.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
